why_how.text: Right of way means that a pedestrian or vehicle has priority to proceed over others in a particular setting.
Yield to a driver who is already at an intersection or reached it before you.
When turning left, yield to drivers approaching in the opposing traffic lane.
If two drivers reach a four-way intersection together, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.
When entering a public highway from a driveway or private road, yield to traffic on the highway.
A driver using an entrance or acceleration ramp must yield to vehicles already on the interstate or limited-access highway.
Yield to pedestrians, bicycle riders and other drivers who remain within the intersection.
Yield the right of way to public-safety vehicles such as emergency, police and fire vehicles.
Yield the right of way to a funeral procession.

why_how.text: Vertical traffic lights usually show red above yellow above green, although some signals are horizontal or show only one color.
At a red light, stop before the intersection and wait behind the stop line, crosswalk or intersection boundary for green.
A yellow traffic light warns that red is next; approach cautiously and prepare to stop.
A green light permits cautious travel through an intersection only when the way is clear.
A green arrow permits a turn in the arrow's direction without first stopping.
At a flashing yellow light, reduce speed and proceed carefully, ready to stop for traffic entering the intersection.
At flashing red, make a complete stop behind the stop line, crosswalk or intersection, then enter only after checking that no traffic crosses your path.
Treat a traffic light that is not operating like a stop sign, yielding and entering the intersection cautiously.

why_how.text: Traffic signs communicate rules, hazards, road location, directions and nearby roadway services.
A sign's shape, color, symbols and wording help identify the kind of information it conveys.
Regulatory signs communicate traffic laws or regulations that govern traffic movement.
Observe the posted school-zone speed restriction during the hours specified on its sign.
A red circle crossed by a slash means that the action represented by the sign is forbidden.
Warning signs alert a driver to potential danger farther along the road.
Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped and yellow, with black symbols or lettering.
